chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Choosing music over radio, and parents warning girls off a musician
summary: As a boy he hesitates between electrician and music; people say musicians amount to nothing and the girls' mothers tell them to avoid him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You know, in looking back on my life in the music business, it certainly had some pitfalls here and there; I can remember the early days when I toring between whether I should get into radio - I had a radio set - I was toring between whether I wanted to be an electrician of some kind - you know - in those days and music. And, of course, music won out but I had to struggle to find my-

self - that's the hard part and I was determined; of course, there was one crack made when I was very young that some-body said I will never amount to a damn - we were talking about that this morning -- that as long as I played a musical instruments, I wouldn't amount to a damn - and, of course, you knew how people thought about musicians and they still do in a way -- I can remember all the kids when I was in the 8th grade, we'll say, and I'm playing around -- I used to--- if it rained in our school and it got dark, I'd get out my banjo and sing and play for the kids and stuff like that and I remember - that all the girls I knew when I first started to play were friendly with me - all the little girls - suddenly, I realized that they all got to become very cold and their mothers said - you stay away from that Davison guy; I hear he is playing in nightclubs and smoking. So, that queered me with all the girls - you know. That's just what I'm trying to put across. So, in those days it was difficult to stay in the music business.
You had to make some sacrifices - didn't you?

Oh, all kinds -- and don't forget how cheap we had to work - oh, man - we worked some places and we'd get a dollar - we thought that was great, you know. And, so, down through the years, as I look back, I stuck it out ---
